All computation lives in `R/`; this notebook runs the scripts in order and shows their results.
The raw Excel exports must be in `data/` (see the README). Long tables are folded away: click
**Show table** to open them. Each table has a **How this table was made** note.

```{r}
#| label: setup
source("R/setup.R")
source("R/load_data.R")
source("R/cleanup.R")
source("R/pupil_table.R")
source("R/direct_path.R")
source("R/stage1.R")
source("R/explained_variance.R")
source("R/cv_models.R")
source("R/goals.R")
source("R/conclusions.R")
source("R/q1_model.R")
source("R/q1_robustness.R")
source("R/q2_analysis.R")

# Tables longer than `collapse_after` rows are folded behind a "Show table" toggle
show_table <- function(x, digits = 3, collapse_after = 15) {
  if (nrow(x) == 0) {
    return(knitr::asis_output("*No rows.*\n"))
  }
  if (nrow(x) <= collapse_after) {
    return(knitr::kable(x, digits = digits))
  }
  html <- knitr::kable(
    x,
    digits = digits, format = "html",
    table.attr = 'class="table table-sm table-striped"'
  )
  knitr::asis_output(paste0(
    "<details><summary>Show table (", nrow(x), " rows)</summary>\n\n", html, "\n\n</details>\n"
  ))
}
```

# Data preparation

## CITO scores that are not numbers

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How this table was made"}
The `Score` column of the Cito workbook (all class sheets stacked) is read as text, decimal
commas are replaced by points and the result is converted to a number. This table lists every
distinct non-empty value that still could not be read as a number. Those scores are treated as
missing everywhere below.
:::

```{r}
show_table(failed_conversion)
```

## CLASS observations with date problems

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How this table was made"}
One row per CLASS observation (`CLASS.xlsx`) whose `Date` could not be read as a date, or whose
date falls in a different quarter than its `Quarter` column (for example a date in March with
`Quarter` = `2023_Q2`). `assessment_date` is the date as read, `expected_quarter` the quarter that
date belongs to. CLASS scores are averaged per school year and class later on, so these rows
are still used, by their school year.
:::

```{r}
show_table(class_date_issues)
```

## Learning-goal scores

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How this table was made"}
One row per learning-goal code (`Leerpadcode`) in the groups 1-2 observations. For every pupil,
all observations of that goal are averaged into one score (scale 0-3, values as recorded); the
columns then summarise those per-pupil averages across pupils: how many pupils have the goal,
and the mean, standard deviation, median, minimum and maximum. Observations from different ages
are mixed, so a goal observed mostly in the first months scores lower than one observed later.
:::

```{r}
show_table(score_summary)
```

## CITO scores

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How this table was made"}
One row per Cito test. For every pupil, all their scores on that test are averaged, over every
grade (3 to 6) and both assessment moments (mid and end of year); the columns summarise those
per-pupil averages across pupils. Cito scores grow with grade and each test has its own scale,
so these numbers describe the export rather than a single moment.
:::

```{r}
show_table(grade_summary)
```

## Extracurricular activities

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How this table was made"}
Number of rows per lesson name in `Extracurricular.xlsx`, over all school years and all
pupils. A row is one pupil taking one lesson in one block, so a pupil who took the same
lesson in several blocks counts several times.
:::

```{r}
data_extra |>
  count(Lesson, sort = TRUE) |>
  show_table()
```

# Pupils, kindergarten time and readiness

One row per pupil (`pupils_table`, built in `R/pupil_table.R`). Of the
`r nrow(pupils_table)` pupils in the master list, `r sum(pupils_table$reached_g3)` have
reached group 3, so their time in kindergarten and readiness are known;
`r sum(pupils_table$reached_g3 & pupils_table$has_cito_g3)` of them also have grade 3 Cito
results (the others started group 3 this school year).

## When group 3 started

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How this table was made"}
For every pupil, the school year in which group 3 started is taken from the first available
source, in this order:

1. **Cito grade 3**: the first school year with a `Grade 3` result (for example
   `mid 2022-2023` gives 2022/23).
2. **Maths tests block 3**: the school year of the first test of a block 3.x
   (`UvA_testresults_math.xlsx`).
3. **Questionnaire group 3**: the school year of the first answer in `Leerjaar` 3.
4. **Current year group**: counted back from the export's school year
   (`r export_school_year`/`r export_school_year + 1`): a pupil now in group *g* started
   group 3 *g* − 3 years ago. This is the only source for pupils who just started group 3.

A pilot on the real data compared these sources, and also the leaving cohort and the last
kindergarten observation: wherever two dated sources (1-3) overlap they give the same year for
every pupil. Counting back (4) and the Cito leaving year are a year behind for a handful of
pupils; those pupils most likely **repeated a year after group 3** and are counted in the last
row. Group 3 is assumed to start on **20 August** of its school year.
:::

```{r}
show_table(g3_sources_overview)
```

## Time in kindergarten

The first table the school asked for: how long pupils spend in kindergarten, how many
started group 3 earlier or later than most children born in the same year, and how old they
are when group 3 starts, with winter birthdays shown separately.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How this table was made"}
**Pupils.** Everyone in the master list who has reached group 3 (see the table above),
including pupils who started group 3 this school year.

**Steps per pupil:**

1. **Start at school**: `Start date` in `Pupils.xlsx`.
2. **Start of group 3**: 20 August of the school year from the table above.
3. **Months in kindergarten** = days from step 1 to step 2, divided by 30.44.
4. **Age at group 3**: age on 20 August of the group 3 year.
5. **Earlier / later than most**: group 3 year minus birth year is the same for most pupils
   (`r pupils_table %>% filter(reached_g3) %>% count(g3_year_offset) %>% slice_max(n, n = 1) %>% pull(g3_year_offset)`
   years). Pupils with one year less started group 3 **earlier than most** children born in the
   same year, pupils with one year more **later than most**. No cut-off date is assumed: the
   school decides per child, and the table below shows how that works out by birth month.

**What the data shows about start dates.** In this export every pupil's `Start date` lies at
or just after their 4th birthday (on average a few days after it), including pupils whose
4th birthday falls before the school opened in 2020. The start date was probably derived from
the (anonymised) birth date. As a result, months in kindergarten is in effect **(age at the
start of group 3 − 4) × 12**: time in kindergarten and age at group 3 cannot be separated in
this data, and the only differences that come from a decision are the pupils who started group
3 earlier or later than most.

**Rows.** All pupils who reached group 3, then the same split by birth quarter, then the pupils
born in October-December (the "autumn children" the school asked about).

**Columns.** `pupils`: number of pupils; `mean_months`, `sd_months`, `min_months`, `max_months`:
months in kindergarten; `group3_earlier_than_most`, `group3_later_than_most`: number of pupils;
`mean_age_at_g3`: average age in years at the start of group 3.

**To check with the school.** How the start date and birth date were anonymised; who decides
when a child moves to group 3, and on what basis; the 20 August start of group 3.
:::

```{r}
show_table(kg_overview, digits = 1)
```

clean switch between two birth months; differences spread over the year point to decisions
per child.

## Goals achieved before group 3

The second table: what share of the goals that matter for group 3 pupils had achieved when
group 3 started.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How this table was made"}
**Goal lists.** From the client's materials: 15 goals marked as important before group 3, and
19 basic goals for groups 1-2.

**Steps per pupil** (pupils who reached group 3):

1. Take all observations of the goals in the list made **before** the pupil's start of group 3
   (20 August of the group 3 year), keeping only scores 0-3.
2. For each goal, keep the **last** observation.
3. A goal counts as **achieved** when that last score is **2 or higher** (2 = the child has some
   notion of the goal, 3 = mastered).
4. The pupil's percentage = achieved goals / goals of the list that were observed. Goals never
   observed for that pupil are left out, not counted as missed.

**Columns.** `goals_in_list`: goals in the client's list; `pupils`: pupils with at least one
of them observed; `mean_pct_achieved`: average of the pupils' percentages; `min_pct`, `max_pct`:
lowest and highest pupil; `p10_pct`, `p90_pct`: 10% of pupils are below / above these values.
:::

```{r}
show_table(goals_overview, digits = 1)
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Conclusion"}
```{r}
#| output: asis
#| echo: false
cat(conclusion_goals())
```
:::

# Q1: kindergarten time and group 3 outcomes

Do pupils who spent longer in kindergarten do better in group 3? Each outcome is compared with
time in kindergarten directly, without looking at what happened in kindergarten itself.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How these tables were made"}
**Pupils.** Pupils who reached group 3 (see "When group 3 started"). Cito outcomes exist only
for pupils with grade 3 Cito results; support in group 3 only when the support file covers that
school year; well-being only for pupils with questionnaire answers in group 3. `n` is the number
of pupils in each model.

**Time in kindergarten.** Months from the start date to the start of group 3 (see "Time in
kindergarten"). In this export that equals the age at the start of group 3 minus 4, so the
estimates are for **more time and an older age at group 3 together**; the data cannot tell
the two apart.

**Outcomes.** *Primary*: Cito ability score (0-5) at the end of group 3 for maths, TMT and
spelling, chosen beforehand because they have the most pupils. *Secondary*: any support record
in group 3 (yes/no) and well-being in group 3 (mean of the 7 questionnaire items, 1-3).
*Few pupils*: reading comprehension in group 3 and Cito at the end of group 4; too few pupils
to conclude anything, shown for completeness.

**Models.** A linear regression per outcome (logistic for support), first without controls,
then with the leaving cohort and the kindergarten class as controls (cohorts took their tests in
different years; the first cohort started when the school opened).

**First table: per 6 extra months in kindergarten.** `estimate` is the change in the outcome
for 6 more months (in ability or well-being points; for support an odds ratio, where 1 means no
difference and above 1 means more support); `ci_low`, `ci_high`: 95% confidence interval; `p`:
p-value; `per_sd`: the estimate divided by the outcome's standard deviation, to compare outcomes
(0.2 is usually called small, 0.5 medium).

**Second table: less than 24 months in kindergarten.** The same, comparing pupils with less
than two years in kindergarten (mostly children born in the autumn) with everyone else.

**Reading the results.** Several outcomes are tested, so a single p-value below .05 can occur by
chance. With about 75 pupils only moderate differences can be detected; the confidence interval
shows which effect sizes the data still allows. Pupils who started group 3 earlier or later than
most were placed on purpose, probably based on how ready they seemed: that can make longer
kindergarten look worse (children kept back may have been behind) or shorter kindergarten look
better (children moved up early may have been ahead).
:::

Per 6 extra months in kindergarten:

```{r}
show_table(direct_months)
```

Less than 24 months in kindergarten (vs 24 or more):

```{r}
show_table(direct_under_24)
```

```{r}

#| fig-height: 4.5
```

# Readiness at the end of kindergarten (Q1 and Q2)

Which groups 1-2 factors go with how many goals a pupil has reached when group 3 starts?
Time in kindergarten answers the first part of Q1 (does more time mean more goals reached?);
the kindergarten class is the closest the data gets to the teaching focus in Q2.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How these tables were made"}
**Pupils.** Pupils who reached group 3, including those who started group 3 this school year
(their kindergarten is complete), with observations before group 3. `n` is the number of pupils
in each model.

**Readiness** (see "Goals achieved before group 3" and `R/pupil_table.R`): for each goal the last
observation before group 3. *Goals before group 3* and *basic goals*: share of the client's goals
at score 2 or higher. *Maths, language, social-emotional, fine and gross motor*: mean of the last
scores (0-3) of all goals in that subject. Most pupils are close to the maximum, so differences
are small and the scale is compressed at the top.

**Factors.**

- *Time in kindergarten*, per 6 months. In this export that is the same as being 6 months older
  at the start of group 3, and teachers' observation scores rise with age, so a positive
  estimate is expected and does not show that the extra time itself helped.
- *Class 1/2b vs 1/2a*: the class the pupil was observed in most. The classes differ in
  teaching focus, but also in teacher and in which children were placed there, so a difference
  cannot be attributed to the teaching focus alone.
- *Lessons per kindergarten year*, per 5 lessons: distinct extracurricular lessons, divided by the
  kindergarten school years the extracurricular file covers (from 2021/22).

**Model.** For each readiness outcome, one linear regression with the three factors together
and the leaving cohort as a control, so each estimate holds the other factors constant.

**Overview table.** Each cell: the estimate in standard deviations of the outcome (0.2 is
usually called small, 0.5 medium) with the 95% interval, `*` when p < .05. The full table below
it gives the estimates in the outcome's own units.

**Support during kindergarten** has its own model (support, time in kindergarten, class and
cohort), on fewer pupils because the support file starts later. Children usually get support
*because* they are behind, so a negative estimate shows who needed help, not that help lowered
readiness.
:::

```{r}
show_table(stage1_overview)
```



# What contributes to the outcomes?

Time in kindergarten is one of several things that differ between pupils in groups 1-2. This
section puts them side by side, in blocks: **time**, **classroom**, **extracurricular lessons**,
**support** and, for the group 3 outcomes, **readiness** at the end of kindergarten. It asks how
much of the differences between pupils each block accounts for.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How this section was made"}
**Pupils.** Pupils who reached group 3 with a kindergarten class (for the goals) or with the
group 3 outcome (for Cito and support). `n` is shown per outcome.

**Features, by block** (each block split into kinds where the data allows):

- *Time*: months in kindergarten (in this export the same as age at group 3 − 4).
- *Classroom*: kindergarten class (1/2b vs 1/2a), and the CLASS total of that class (average of
  emotional support, classroom organization and instructional support), averaged over the
  pupil's kindergarten years. The three CLASS domains are measured on the same class-years and
  move together too closely to be told apart, so they are combined.
- *Extracurricular*: distinct lessons per kindergarten year, by kind of lesson (sport &
  movement, arts & culture, technology, science & strategy, language & numbers, life skills &
  play; see "Lesson categories"). Kinds nobody took in kindergarten are left out.
- *Support*: any support during kindergarten, by kind of need (language, learning, other:
  behaviour, motor skills, assessment). For the first cohorts the support file covers none of
  their kindergarten years, so they count as without support; the cohort control keeps this
  from looking like an effect.
- *Readiness* (group 3 outcomes only): last observation scores per subject (maths, language,
  social-emotional, motor), **compared with classmates** (standardised within each kindergarten
  class), because the two classes' teachers score differently (see the readiness section).

**Models.** One linear regression per outcome with all features and the leaving cohort as a
control; support in group 3 (yes/no) as a linear probability model. Continuous features and the
outcome are in standard deviations, so the fit coefficients are comparable: the change in the
outcome (in SD) per SD of the feature, or between the two groups for yes/no features.

**Explained variance per block.** The model is refitted with every combination of blocks. A
block's *share* is how much it adds to the explained variance (R², on top of cohort), averaged
over every order in which the blocks can be added; the shares add up to the model's total.
*Lost without block* is how much R² drops when only that block is removed. The 95% intervals come
from refitting on 300 resamples of the pupils. A resample always finds some R² by chance, so these
intervals sit somewhat high (a share can even fall just below its own interval); compare with the
chance level below.

**Chance level.** With about 75 pupils, a block gets some R² even if it has nothing to do with the
outcome, and more so the more features it has. The *noise level* is a block's average share when
the outcome is shuffled (300 times), so that nothing can truly be explained; *above noise* is the
share minus that level. Only shares clearly above the noise level mean something.

**Two framings for the group 3 outcomes.** *Kindergarten factors*: time, classroom,
extracurricular, support. *Kindergarten factors + readiness*: adds what the child could do at the
end of kindergarten. Readiness is partly a result of the other blocks, so in the second framing
it takes over part of their share.

**Reading the results.** These are associations, not effects: pupils were not assigned to more
time, a class or support at random. The shares describe which differences between pupils go
together with differences in the outcome.
:::

# Which goals matter? (Q2)

In the explained-variance section, readiness at the end of kindergarten accounted for
`r paste0(sub(", end of group 3", "", filter(ev_variance_table, block == "Readiness", outcome %in% goals_cito_tests)$outcome), " ", fmt(filter(ev_variance_table, block == "Readiness", outcome %in% goals_cito_tests)$r2_share), collapse = ", ")`
of the variance in group 3 Cito. Those shares describe the pupils the models were fitted on.
This section checks how much of it holds for pupils a model has not seen, and looks inside the
readiness block at three levels: which subjects, which learning domains within them, and which
of the school's 15 goals before group 3 carry it.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How this section was made"}
**Class check.** For maths readiness (scored by the teachers) and for each group 3 Cito test: the
difference between class 1/2b and 1/2a in standard deviations, with the leaving cohort as a
control. If the classes differ on readiness but not on Cito, the readiness difference is in how
the teachers score, which is why readiness is compared with classmates everywhere else.

**Models.** The cross-validated elastic net from the original Q2 analysis (`R/cv_models.R`):
missing values filled with the training folds' median and features standardised inside each
training split, the penalty chosen by an inner 5-fold split, 5 folds repeated 10 times (50 fits per
model and test). Six models, each adding one block, the same blocks as in the explained-variance
section: *average only*; *cohort*; *+ kindergarten factors* (time, classroom, extracurricular,
support); *+ readiness by subject* (maths, language, social-emotional, motor, compared with
classmates); *+ readiness by domain* (the learning domains of those subjects, see "Learning
domains"); *+ readiness by goal* (the last score before group 3 on each of the 15 goals before
group 3, minus the class average). The cohort model is an ordinary regression, the others the
elastic net.

**Learning domains.** The `Domein` column mixes short codes and full Dutch names for the same
domains across school years, so the domain is taken from the goal code instead: the letters before
its first digit (`TG7.3_E1` → `TG`). Names come from a list in `R/goals.R` built from the
`Translations` sheet and the goal descriptions; the subject is the one most of the domain's
observations are recorded under. A domain enters the models when it belongs to maths, language,
social-emotional or motor development and is observed for at least half of the pupils who reached
group 3. Its readiness is the mean of the last scores before group 3 over its goals, standardised
within each kindergarten class.

**Prediction table.** `mean_rmse`: prediction error for left-out pupils in Cito ability points;
`predicted_r2`: share of the variance predicted for left-out pupils (0 = no better than the
average, below 0 = worse), with the 10th-90th percentile over the 10 repeats; `in_sample_r2`: the
R² of the same blocks in the explained-variance section, fitted on all pupils.

**Selection.** For the domain model (subjects and domains) and for the model with all blocks
(goals), how often each feature has a non-zero coefficient across the 50 fits, and whether it is
mostly positive when kept. Kept often means a stable
predictor; it is not a test of significance. Goals that almost every pupil masters vary little
and are rarely kept, which does not make them unimportant.
:::

# Q1 as first reported: time in kindergarten × extracurricular activities

Development is the average z-score across learning goals per pupil.
Both predictors are mean-centred, so each main effect is the effect at the average of the other predictor.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How this table and model were made"}
**Development.** For every pupil and goal, all observations are averaged; each goal's averages
are turned into z-scores across pupils; a pupil's development is the mean of their z-scores.
0 is average, above 0 above average.

**Activities.** Number of distinct lesson names a pupil took in `Extracurricular.xlsx`, over all
school years. Pupils without any record are missing (not 0) and drop out of the model.

**Kindergarten months.** `kindergarten_months` from `cleanup.R`: months from the start date to
1 August two school years after the school year of the start, or to today if that is later than
today. This is not the time until group 3 actually started (see the robustness section).

**Stages.** `data_clean`: pupils in the master list; `with learning-goal scores`: pupils with a
development score; `complete cases in model`: those with kindergarten months and activities too.

**Model.** Linear regression of development on kindergarten months, activities and their
product, both predictors centred on their mean.
:::

```{r}
show_table(q1_sample_sizes)
```

```{r}
summary(m_q1)
confint(m_q1)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
q1_plot
```

## Robustness of the activities effect

The model above changes one thing at a time, from the reported specification towards
pupils who reached group 3, their actual time until group 3, and the transition goals
achieved before group 3. If the activities coefficient changes sign or vanishes at a
step, that choice drives the result. `b_per_sd_outcome` puts the outcomes on one scale.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How this table was made"}
Each row refits the regression of the section above with one more change than the row before:

1. The model as reported.
2. Pupils without an extracurricular record get 0 activities instead of being dropped.
3. Adds months in school (from the start date to the last observation in the export) as a
   control, so older and younger pupils are compared at the same time in school.
4. Keeps only pupils who reached group 3.
5. Replaces `kindergarten_months` with months until group 3 actually started (as in the
   kindergarten table above).
6. Replaces development with the share of the 15 goals before group 3 achieved on the last
   observation before group 3 (as in the goals table above).

**Columns.** `n`: pupils in the model; `activities_b`: change in the outcome per extra activity,
at average kindergarten time; `ci_low`, `ci_high`: 95% confidence interval; `p`: p-value;
`b_per_sd_outcome`: `activities_b` divided by the outcome's standard deviation, so rows with
different outcomes can be compared.
:::

```{r}
show_table(q1_bridge, digits = 4)
```

Spearman correlation between transition goals achieved and activities (step 6 sample):
rho = `r round(q1_bridge_rho$estimate, 2)`, p = `r signif(q1_bridge_rho$p.value, 2)`.

`kindergarten_months` (from `cleanup.R`) counts from the start date to 1 August two
school years later. For pupils who reached group 3 it can be compared with the months
until group 3 actually started:

# Q2 as first reported

The first Q2 analysis (`R/q2_analysis.R`) predicted group 3 Cito from observation scores per
subject with the cross-validated elastic net, and picked two subjects per test for simpler
models. The "Which goals matter?" section above reuses the same elastic net, with corrected inputs:

- observation scores as the **last score before group 3**, compared with classmates, instead of the
  average of all observations at any age;
- **months until group 3 started** instead of `kindergarten_months` (see the robustness section);
- support **during kindergarten** instead of support records from all years, which included
  support given after the outcome;
- the **end-of-group-3 Cito ability score** instead of the average of mid and end scores.

It also originally read only the first Cito sheet (one cohort, 18 pupils per test); that is
fixed for both analyses.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Original results (all subjects, elastic net)"}
